correctness.rationale: All balanced tournament edge-sign vectors lie in the complete-graph circulation subspace. Explicit cyclic tournament 3-cycle flips realize an integral triangle basis of differences; this establishes full affine span under any strictly positive sample law. Intersection with the graphic cut space proves every selected nullity. Fundamental-cycle unimodularity, Cauchy-Binet and Cayley count prove the exact weighted determinant formula. Permutation symmetry plus balance proves the full uniform covariance, while matching swaps and spherical fourth-moment comparison prove the remaining properties. Replayed exact SymPy checker confirms the order-three/order-five cases including all order-five maximal candidate selections under two full-support laws. Computations are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: Regular tournaments model balanced round-robin comparison outcomes. Recovering edge signs under the score constraints is a canonical degree-one Fourier acquisition problem. The theorem completely determines which coordinate subsets lose information, identifies and counts all largest independent sets, proves a design-volume equality robust to arbitrary positive sampling weights, and establishes tightness, matching independence and exact 3-design strength for the uniform ensemble. These are motivated structural properties rather than a small parameter-table increment.
